quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, release the gas pedal first to slow down. If you need to slow more, gently and steadily press the brake pedal.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What is true about a driver who drives much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: They are a very safe driver.
They should not let other cars pass.
They may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-way road, if traffic backs up behind you because you are driving too slowly, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When do roads freeze most quickly?
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded parts of roads under trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: What happens when you mix drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces alcohol's effect on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medicines) can harm your brain function and impair your driving. Mixing alcohol with other drugs greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit in school zones?
questions.explanation: Unless a different speed limit is posted, the speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive carefully in school zones because children and other pedestrians may enter the roadway.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed you can drive?

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and prudent.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and prudent. Adjust your speed based on the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. You must also stay within posted speed limits.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your turn signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal every time you change lanes.

questions.question: What must you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching?

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move immediately to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers must be able to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. As speed increases, you must stay extra alert for hazards.

questions.question: When does Massachusetts law require you to use your headlights?

options.text: During the day in good weather.
When the temperature is below freezing.

questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights to be on when driving in tunnels. Headlights help you see better in areas with low visibility.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and the actions of other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: After you stop for a school bus that is letting children off, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the children to wave before driving.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Watch for children walking on the side of the road after a school bus stops with its lights flashing and stop arm out. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway ahead is under maintenance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead is under maintenance.
questions.explanation: Construction signs are orange with black markings. They warn you of dangerous conditions in work areas. This sign tells you that construction is ahead and you should slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What is important to remember when driving on wet pavement?

options.text: Pavement is very slippery right after rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires lose grip on the thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain or on roads with standing water or slush.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to drive safely over the hill.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: As safe as driving in other conditions.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying full attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Higher speeds make tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Shallow water is more dangerous than deep water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Higher speeds make tires less effective.
questions.explanation: On a wet road, your tires work less well as you drive faster. At very high speeds, your tires cannot remove water from the road. Your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other objects on the roadside.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder for drivers to see at night than during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever objects are not visible for 500 feet, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: When can you carefully drive through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue carefully through it.
